personalInfo.name: Peng Lu
personalInfo.role: Research-driven UX and Service & System Designer
personalInfo.description: Research-driven UX and Service & System Designer with PhD training in design research. My work focuses on understanding complex socio-technical systems and human experience dynamics through quali-quantitative research, analytical framework development, and system-level analysis. I am particularly interested in translating research insights into service design and experience-informed decision-making.

workExperience.title: PhD Researcher
achievements: Conducted long-term quali-quantitative research on human–technology interaction and user experience in complex socio-technical systems.
Designed and applied phenomenological research methods, including experience sampling and in-depth interviews.
Developed analytical frameworks and conceptual models to interpret experiential data.
Communicated research insights to interdisciplinary audiences to support discussions on system design, innovation, and experience-oriented improvement.

workExperience.title: Design Researcher Intern
achievements: Engaged with professional designers to observe and understand industry design processes, constraints, and decision-making practices.
Analyzed service and product development workflows to identify opportunities for research-informed design reflection.
Provided research-based perspectives to internal discussions, supporting design reasoning rather than direct solution delivery.

workExperience.title: Service Design & Management Thesis Intern
achievements: Analyzed patient flow and service processes using quantitative, time-based operational data within a highly regulated healthcare context.
Applied service design tools such as service blueprints and system maps to structure findings and communicate insights.
Identified bottlenecks and prolonged service phases to support internal reflection on service efficiency and organization.

achievements.title: Doctoral Research on Human–Vehicle Interaction
achievements.subtitle: Conceptual frameworks and experiential analysis of co-driving pleasure and human–vehicle relations.

education.title: Ph.D. in Design, Politecnico di Milano

education.title: M.Sc. in Product-Service System Design and Management Engineering, Politecnico di Milano
